messages:
Maya: quick check — before I open the RFC: can we change the default fallback order for model routing? current behavior falls back to 'closest-tier' then 'cheapest'. wondering if we should invert for latency-sensitive routes.
Luca: what's the exact API surface we'd change? the endpoint is /v1/generate? params: `model_id`, `routing.hints` and `routing.fallback_order` (optional today).
James: we discussed this in sync — safe to change if we keep backward-compatibility for 2 release cycles. suggest adding an explicit `routing.fallback_policy` enum instead of flipping semantics silently.
Maya: yes, I want to avoid surprise regressions. can we accept both old `fallback_order` array and new `fallback_policy` string for a deprecation window?
Ravi: +1. implementation plan: server will accept both; if `fallback_policy` present it wins. add a server-side lint warning when `fallback_order` is used.
Luca: prototype of payload I have in my branch:
```json
{
  "model_id": "redwood/long-8b",
  "routing": {
    "hints": ["region:eu-west", "tier:premium"],
    "fallback_policy": "latency-first" // other: "cost-first", "balanced"
  }
}
```
This would default hosted routes to `latency-first` for chat and `cost-first` for background embeddings unless overridden.
Sara: small SDK note — the python client exposes `routing` as a dict. we'll need to map `fallback_order` -> `fallback_policy` and emit DeprecationWarning. I can prep the PR.
James: tests: please add contract tests verifying both shapes and that response header `x-routing-used` indicates which model was selected. we should also make sure the JSON response doesn't change shape.
Maya: good call on header. response format must stay stable — only add optional `routing_debug` field under `meta` when `?debug=true`. no breaking changes to `choices` or `output`.
Ravi: ops considerations — Dedicated customers might have pinned model versions. fallback_policy should respect `customer.model_pin` and not route to a different model family. add a guard.
Luca: noted. I'll add a check that pins override routing hints and we log a metric when a pin prevents fallback.
ci-bot: CI: ran contract tests on branch `luca/routing-policy`. 86/89 passed, 3 flaky tests failing in `test_batching_edgecases`.
Maya: ok can we get CI green before merge. Ravi, can you take a look at the pin guard in the next 2hrs? tagging you @Ravi.
Ravi: I can do a quick review. if green we'll canary this on dedicated-us-east and hosted-eu on Wednesday.
James: also add a migration note for customers: announce in release notes and console banner for 30 days.
Sara: PR link: <https://git.internal/redwood/p/redwood-api/pull/342> — adding SDK deprecation patch and tests now.
Maya: perfect. final checklist: (1) server accepts both shapes, (2) SDK warns and maps, (3) contract tests cover response stability, (4) telemetry for pin overrides, (5) release note + console banner. anyone object?
Luca: no objections. I'll queue the canary plan. :shipit:
James: ping me for code review before merge.
Maya: thanks all — I'll file the RFC today with those decisions and link the PRs here.
